Section 1 · Decision snapshot

The contact-routing problem is real and measured — but do not commit to a Charter until the cost-per-contact and volume gaps are closed.

Discover verdict
RESHAPE — the problem is real; shape it, but the case is not yet sizeable

2 kill trigger(s) fired with a reshape effect — the Move may advance only once the fix conditions are met. The opportunity can be stated, but not yet sized to the standard a CFO gate requires.

Problem statementContact-centre containment sits at 28% against a 40% target while average handle time is rising (7.2 min, up from 6.4) — easy contacts are deflected, leaving agents the hard ones, so cost-to-serve and repeat-transfer (18.4%) are climbing without a routing intelligence layer.
Next evidence requestCapture the cost-per-contact baseline and the annual contact volume — the two evidence asks that gate an honest Charter business case.
So whatDiscover can advance to Charter as a shaping exercise — but the opportunity cannot be sized to a CFO standard until two seed gaps close.
Decision roleDecide whether the idea is real enough to shape into a Charter.

Contact Center AI Routing·Pain and opportunity
Slide 4 / 7
Section 3 · Pain and opportunity

There is real value in lifting containment and cutting repeat transfers — but it can only be stated directionally until the monetization inputs land.

The pain is real and measured: containment is stuck, handle time is rising and repeat transfers are high. The value is genuine — but with the monetization inputs missing it can only be stated directionally, never as a dollar figure.

Pain themes and the constraints that bound the solution space
Containment is plateaued while handle time rises
Containment sits at 28% against a 40% target; AHT is up to 7.2 min from 6.4. Easy contacts are deflected, so the calls that reach agents are harder — the two metrics must be modelled together.
No slack to absorb the mix shift
Labour-takeout value is sized as if freed hours convert to savings, while agent utilization is already above target — there is no slack to harvest.
Repeat transfers read as mis-routing
Repeat transfers run at 18.4% — consistent with routing that does not place contacts with the right-skilled agent first time.
Known constraints
  • WFM lead is on record for agent-assist, not full deflection — autonomy beyond assist is out of the honest solution space.
  • A transcript-use privacy review is pending — customer-facing inference is conditional on it clearing.
  • Agent utilisation at 84% is above the 80% target — labour-takeout value is capped by the lack of capacity headroom.
Opportunity statement

Lifting containment 28% → 40% with intelligent routing and agent assist would re-route the easy-contact load away from agents and cut repeat transfers — but the opportunity can only be stated directionally until annual contact volume and cost-per-contact are recorded.

So whatA directional opportunity is enough to justify a shaping Charter — it is not enough to justify build funding.
Decision roleConfirm the opportunity is worth shaping, and how honestly it can be expressed.
OwnerPriya Iyer (Program Lead)
